feedback: The perfect passive infinitive places the painting before the present appearance and makes the wall its receiver.
This active perfect form would make the wall perform the painting.
This makes the wall the painter and presents an action in progress now.
Appear does not take this -ing clause directly as its complement.

questions.setup: Rewrite the sentence without changing who performs the action.
questions.prompt: 'It is important that visitors keep their tickets.' It is important ___ their tickets.
options: visitors keeping
for visitors keeping
for visitors to keep
for visitors to keeping
questions.explanation: For introduces the subject of the infinitive, making visitors the people who must keep the tickets.
feedback: This does not supply the standard for-plus-subject infinitive after important in the given frame.
After the subject visitors in this for-clause, use to keep.
For introduces the subject of the infinitive, making visitors the people who must keep the tickets.
An infinitival to takes keep rather than keeping.

questions.setup: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar, preserving both familiarity and a recurring requirement.
questions.prompt: As a freelance translator, Hana is accustomed to ___ her choice of words to clients.
options: have to justify
having to justify
having justify
to have justified
questions.explanation: Accustomed to takes an -ing complement; having to justify expresses the recurring requirement within it.
feedback: The preposition to after accustomed needs having, not have.
Accustomed to takes an -ing complement; having to justify expresses the recurring requirement within it.
Have to requires to before justify, even when have becomes having.
The existing to is prepositional; adding a perfect infinitive does not form the required complement.

questions.setup: Choose the rewrite preserving the committee's own undertaking.
questions.prompt: 'The committee is committed to publishing the evidence.'
options: The committee has compelled someone to publish the evidence.
The committee has undertaken to publish the evidence.
The committee has acknowledged publishing the evidence.
The committee has objected to publishing the evidence.
questions.explanation: Both expressions attribute the intended publishing to the committee, despite their different complement forms.
feedback: This adds a different performer and coercion, neither of which the commitment states.
Both expressions attribute the intended publishing to the committee, despite their different complement forms.
Acknowledged publishing reports an admission about an action, not an undertaking to perform it.
Objected to reverses the committee's commitment by expressing opposition.

questions.setup: Rewrite the purpose using the supplied noun phrase and correct grammar.
questions.prompt: 'The scheme aims to reduce queues.' The scheme was introduced with the aim ___.
options: to reducing queues
of reduce queues
of reducing queues
of to reduce queues
questions.explanation: Changing aims to into with the aim of changes the following action to an -ing clause.
feedback: The noun phrase with the aim takes of reducing in this construction.
After of, use reducing rather than the basic verb reduce.
Changing aims to into with the aim of changes the following action to an -ing clause.
A to-infinitive cannot directly follow of here.

questions.setup: During the interview, the host repeatedly asked a researcher to defend a colleague's views. Interpret the researcher's response as described below.
questions.prompt: 'She resisted being drawn into defending arguments she did not share.'
options: She defended the host against pressure from the colleague.
She denied that the colleague had expressed those arguments.
She opposed pressure to become the defender of those arguments.
She tried to draw her colleague into defending her own arguments.
questions.explanation: Being drawn makes her the receiver of pressure; defending names the activity she was being pressed to undertake.
feedback: The researcher is the person pressured; the host and colleague are not described as needing her defense.
Resisting participation is not denying that the arguments existed.
Being drawn makes her the receiver of pressure; defending names the activity she was being pressed to undertake.
The passive being drawn makes her the target of pressure, not its source.

questions.setup: Read the statement without adding an assumption about effort or intention.
questions.prompt: 'The report failed to address the main objection.'
options: The writer attempted a response but lacked the ability to complete it.
The writer deliberately refused to respond to the objection.
The report discussed the objection but reached an incorrect conclusion.
The report did not address the objection; the statement does not explain why.
questions.explanation: Fail to can report that something did not happen without specifying whether it was attempted, forgotten, or deliberately omitted.
feedback: Failed to address establishes the omission but does not itself establish an attempt or inability.
A deliberate refusal is one possible cause, but the sentence does not establish it.
Failing to address the objection is different from addressing it unsuccessfully on the merits.
Fail to can report that something did not happen without specifying whether it was attempted, forgotten, or deliberately omitted.

questions.setup: A witness's account is being summarized. Choose what the sentence itself establishes.
questions.prompt: 'The witness denied having disclosed the password.'
options: The witness had disclosed it and then regretted doing so.
The witness promised not to disclose it in the future.
The investigator proved that the witness had kept it confidential.
The witness rejected the claim that they had disclosed it.
questions.explanation: Denied reports the witness's position; having disclosed locates the disputed action before the denial without proving whether it happened.
feedback: A denial does not establish the alleged disclosure or express regret about it.
Having disclosed concerns an earlier alleged action, not a future undertaking.
Reporting a denial is not independent proof that the disclosure did not happen.
Denied reports the witness's position; having disclosed locates the disputed action before the denial without proving whether it happened.

questions.setup: Choose who will make the call in each sentence.
questions.prompt: (1) Elena promised Mark to call the supplier. (2) Elena persuaded Mark to call the supplier.
options: Mark in (1); Elena in (2).
Mark in both sentences.
Elena in (1); Mark in (2).
Elena in both sentences.
questions.explanation: Promise links the infinitive to the person promising; persuade links it to the person persuaded.
feedback: This reverses the two verbs' patterns: Mark receives the promise but is the caller after persuade.
The person receiving a promise is not necessarily the performer of its action; Elena is the caller in (1).
Promise links the infinitive to the person promising; persuade links it to the person persuaded.
Elena persuades in (2), but Mark performs the action she persuades him to undertake.

questions.setup: Rewrite the report while preserving its source and earlier time reference.
questions.prompt: 'It appears that the figures were altered before publication.' The figures appear ___.
options: to alter before publication
to be altering before publication
to have been altered before publication
having been altered before publication
questions.explanation: The perfect passive infinitive preserves the earlier alteration while appear retains the source's tentative assessment.
feedback: This makes the figures perform an action rather than receive an earlier alteration.
This is active and ongoing, not an earlier completed passive action.
The perfect passive infinitive preserves the earlier alteration while appear retains the source's tentative assessment.
Appear requires an infinitive complement in this rewrite, not a direct -ing clause.

questions.setup: Choose the participants in the remembered scene.
questions.prompt: 'I remember seeing Amira help the visitor lift the case.'
options: Amira watched the speaker assist the visitor with the case.
The speaker watched Amira assist the visitor with the case.
The visitor watched Amira and the speaker lift the case.
The speaker remembers intending to help Amira find a visitor.
questions.explanation: Remember seeing gives the speaker's memory; Amira performs help, and the visitor is assisted with lifting.
feedback: I is the person remembering and seeing; Amira is the helper observed.
Remember seeing gives the speaker's memory; Amira performs help, and the visitor is assisted with lifting.
The visitor is the person helped, not the observer identified by the sentence.
Seeing reports an observed scene, and help the visitor lift is not an intention to find someone.

questions.setup: The historian was not consulted before publication and now regrets that exclusion. Choose the phrase preserving these facts.
questions.prompt: She regrets ___ before the biography appeared.
options: not having consulted
to have been consulted
having been consulted
not having been consulted
questions.explanation: Not negates the earlier passive event; the perfect gerund places the missing consultation before publication.
feedback: This makes her the person who failed to consult someone else.
Regret about an earlier event takes an -ing complement, and this also loses the negation.
This says consultation occurred and was regretted, reversing the stated exclusion.
Not negates the earlier passive event; the perfect gerund places the missing consultation before publication.

questions.setup: Choose the pair of standard forms that both express a need for someone to inspect the wiring.
questions.prompt: The wiring needs ___.
options: checking / to be checked
to check / checking
being check / to be checked
to checking / checked
questions.explanation: Need checking and need to be checked both give the wiring a passive role.
feedback: Need checking and need to be checked both give the wiring a passive role.
Checking works, but to check would make the wiring perform the inspection.
To be checked works, but the passive -ing form would require checked after being.
To checking is incorrect here, so this pair cannot be accepted. Checking and to be checked are the two alternatives in the correct pair.

questions.setup: Choose who is scheduled to meet the delegation.
questions.prompt: 'Rosa arranged for Ibrahim to meet the delegation at the station.'
options: Rosa, with Ibrahim organizing the meeting.
Rosa and Ibrahim, both explicitly required to attend.
The delegation, which arranged to collect Rosa.
Ibrahim, with Rosa organizing the meeting.
questions.explanation: Arrange for + person + to + verb identifies a performer distinct from the organizer.
feedback: Rosa is the subject of arranged; Ibrahim is the subject introduced by for before to meet.
The sentence names Ibrahim as the person meeting them; it does not state that Rosa will attend.
The delegation is the object of meet and is not described as making the arrangement.
Arrange for + person + to + verb identifies a performer distinct from the organizer.

questions.setup: Choose the paraphrase preserving the speaker's assessment.
questions.prompt: 'The engineer was too cautious to dismiss the crack as cosmetic.'
options: She dismissed the crack because her caution was excessive.
She needed more caution before she would be permitted to dismiss the crack.
Her caution prevented her from simply dismissing the crack.
She cautiously dismissed the crack after establishing its cause.
questions.explanation: Too + adjective + to + verb can describe a degree of a quality that prevents the action.
feedback: Too cautious to dismiss presents caution as an obstacle to dismissal, not its cause.
The sentence does not describe a permission threshold or insufficient caution.
Too + adjective + to + verb can describe a degree of a quality that prevents the action.
This asserts the dismissal that the original presents as prevented by caution.

questions.setup: Read the travel account. Choose the function of the infinitive at the end.
questions.prompt: 'After driving for six hours, we reached the venue, only to discover that the event had been cancelled.'
options: It states the purpose for which the group drove to the venue.
It presents an unwelcome discovery after the arrival.
It describes a discovery the group avoided making.
It reports the group's earlier reason for cancelling the event.
questions.explanation: Only to + verb can introduce an unexpected or disappointing result following an action.
feedback: Only to discover presents the outcome, not a purpose of travelling there to learn of cancellation.
Only to + verb can introduce an unexpected or disappointing result following an action.
The account states that they did discover the cancellation.
The group discovers a prior cancellation; it is not described as having caused it.

questions.setup: The assistant can solve the problem without help. Choose the completion preserving the solver and the manageable level of difficulty.
questions.prompt: The problem is simple enough ___ independently.
options: for the assistant to be solved
for the assistant to solve
the assistant solving
for solving the assistant
questions.explanation: For identifies the solver; the problem is understood as the object of solve after enough.
feedback: This makes the assistant, rather than the problem, the thing being solved.
For identifies the solver; the problem is understood as the object of solve after enough.
This does not form the required for-plus-subject infinitive after enough.
This makes the assistant the object of solving and loses the intended actor.

questions.setup: A newspaper reports an allegation without independently confirming it. Choose the rewrite preserving that distance.
questions.prompt: 'Investigators are said to have recovered a second recording.'
options: Investigators say that they will recover a second recording.
Investigators have confirmed that a second recording was recovered.
Investigators were instructed to recover a second recording.
It is said that investigators recovered a second recording.
questions.explanation: Both structures attribute the report to an unspecified source; the perfect infinitive places recovery before the reporting.
feedback: This makes investigators the source and moves recovery into the future.
This adds confirmation and identifies a source not established in the original.
An instruction is different from a report that recovery has occurred.
Both structures attribute the report to an unspecified source; the perfect infinitive places recovery before the reporting.

questions.setup: Read only what the report states. Choose the supported conclusion.
questions.prompt: 'Even the senior analyst had difficulty distinguishing noise from a real signal.'
options: The distinction was difficult for the analyst; success is not specified.
The analyst failed to identify any real signal.
The analyst was unable to explain a distinction that was easy to recognize.
The analyst eventually distinguished the signals without effort.
questions.explanation: Have difficulty + -ing describes trouble performing an action without by itself settling whether it was completed successfully.
feedback: Have difficulty + -ing describes trouble performing an action without by itself settling whether it was completed successfully.
Difficulty does not establish failure; the analyst may have succeeded with effort.
The sentence concerns distinguishing the signals, not explaining a distinction already made.
Without effort conflicts with the stated difficulty, and eventual success is not reported.

questions.setup: Choose the rewrite that preserves a general permission to record, without requiring recording or specifying who must do it.
questions.prompt: 'The policy permits recording in the foyer.'
options: The policy allows people to record in the foyer.
The policy requires people to record in the foyer.
The policy allows staff to prevent people from recording in the foyer.
The policy requires individual approval before recording in the foyer.
questions.explanation: Permits recording can be rewritten with an explicit generic actor followed by allows ... to record.
feedback: Permits recording can be rewritten with an explicit generic actor followed by allows ... to record.
Requires changes permission into an obligation.
This authorizes staff to stop the action, rather than permitting the action itself.
This adds an approval condition that the original general permission does not state.

questions.setup: The speaker has already read the report several times. Interpret this comment after another reading.
questions.prompt: 'I can't help wondering whether one assumption has been overlooked.'
options: The question keeps occurring to the speaker and is hard to avoid.
The speaker cannot assist someone else in identifying the missing assumption.
The speaker has proved that the assumption was omitted.
The speaker refuses to consider the possibility of an omitted assumption.
questions.explanation: Can't help + -ing can describe an involuntary or hard-to-avoid thought or reaction; wondering still leaves the answer open.
feedback: Can't help + -ing can describe an involuntary or hard-to-avoid thought or reaction; wondering still leaves the answer open.
Can't help + -ing here means cannot avoid the thought, not inability to provide assistance.
Wondering raises a question; it does not establish that an omission occurred.
The phrase says the thought persists, not that it is rejected.

questions.setup: An editor wants to preserve the fact that the reviewer did not notice a change. Choose the equivalent sentence.
questions.prompt: 'The change escaped the reviewer's notice.'
options: The reviewer failed to notice the change.
The reviewer avoided noticing the change.
The reviewer regretted noticing the change.
The reviewer remembered noticing the change.
questions.explanation: Both sentences state that the reviewer did not notice it; fail to provides an infinitive-based equivalent.
feedback: Both sentences state that the reviewer did not notice it; fail to provides an infinitive-based equivalent.
Avoided suggests prevention or deliberate avoidance that the original does not establish.
This says the reviewer noticed it and regretted doing so, reversing the fact.
This presents noticing as an earlier experience the reviewer recalls, reversing the stated non-occurrence.

questions.setup: A draft names Rowan as the project's sole designer. A colleague reads the objection below. Choose its precise target.
questions.prompt: 'I object to Rowan's being credited with the entire design.'
options: The attribution of all the design work to Rowan.
Rowan's refusal to credit the other designers.
The speaker's having designed the project without Rowan.
Rowan's objection to being named in the project report.
questions.explanation: Rowan's is the subject of the passive gerund clause; the objection concerns credit being assigned to Rowan.
feedback: Rowan's is the subject of the passive gerund clause; the objection concerns credit being assigned to Rowan.
Rowan is the recipient of credit in being credited; the sentence does not say Rowan controls the attribution.
No such authorship claim is made; the disputed matter is the attribution described by the gerund clause.
The speaker objects; Rowan is not presented as the person raising the objection.

questions.setup: Compare (1) 'The author acknowledged overstating the claim in last year's paper' and (2) 'The author acknowledged having overstated the claim in last year's paper.'
questions.prompt: Which distinction between the two complements is warranted?
options: The first describes a continuing habit, whereas the second describes an earlier completed act.
Both can describe the same earlier act; the perfect form marks its priority explicitly.
The first leaves the author's responsibility open, whereas the second explicitly assigns it to the author.
The first reports an admission, whereas the second gives independent proof that the claim was overstated.
questions.explanation: The dated paper supplies past reference for the simple gerund; 'having overstated' additionally marks the act as earlier than the acknowledgment.
feedback: The simple gerund can name the single earlier overstatement in the dated paper; it need not describe a habit.
The dated paper supplies past reference for the simple gerund; 'having overstated' additionally marks the act as earlier than the acknowledgment.
The author is understood as the person responsible for overstating in both complements; perfect form does not change that role.
Both are reports of acknowledgment; the perfect gerund adds relative timing, not independent verification.

questions.setup: Read the summary of the review. Choose what its wording establishes.
questions.prompt: 'The review identifies serious weaknesses but stops short of recommending withdrawal.'
options: It recommends withdrawal after listing the weaknesses.
It begins a recommendation of withdrawal but leaves the sentence unfinished.
It does not go as far as recommending withdrawal.
It recommends postponing withdrawal until weaknesses are repaired.
questions.explanation: Stop short of + -ing identifies a step or claim that is not taken despite movement in that direction.
feedback: Stops short of places the review before that step, not at it.
The expression marks a limit to the position taken, not an incomplete sentence.
Stop short of + -ing identifies a step or claim that is not taken despite movement in that direction.
No timing recommendation follows from not recommending withdrawal.

questions.setup: A journalist asks whether closure is impossible. The spokesperson's response is summarized below. Choose what can be concluded.
questions.prompt: 'The spokesperson declined to rule out closing the branch.'
options: The spokesperson confirmed that the branch would close.
The spokesperson rejected closure as an acceptable option.
The spokesperson did not exclude closure as an option.
The spokesperson promised that the branch would remain open.
questions.explanation: Declined to rule out withholds an exclusion; closing names the option that remains unexcluded.
feedback: Refusing to exclude closure is not a confirmation that it will happen.
That reverses the effect of declining to rule it out.
Declined to rule out withholds an exclusion; closing names the option that remains unexcluded.
A promise to remain open would exclude the outcome the spokesperson declines to rule out.

questions.setup: Choose the rewrite preserving the memo's recommendation without asserting that examination has already occurred.
questions.prompt: 'The memo recommends not leaving the discrepancy unexamined.'
options: The memo confirms that the discrepancy has been examined.
The memo recommends leaving the discrepancy as it stands.
The memo recommends examining the discrepancy.
The memo recommends avoiding further examination of the discrepancy.
questions.explanation: Not leaving it unexamined recommends an examination; the negative wording does not reverse that advice.
feedback: A recommendation does not establish that the recommended action was completed.
Leaving it as it stands loses the instruction to examine it.
Not leaving it unexamined recommends an examination; the negative wording does not reverse that advice.
Avoiding examination contradicts the recommendation against leaving it unexamined.

questions.setup: The client received the revised estimate only after approving the work. Interpret the complaint.
questions.prompt: 'She objected to not being told about the price increase beforehand.'
options: She objects to having disclosed the increase herself.
Her objection concerns the earlier failure to inform her.
She wants the contractor to withhold the increase from other clients.
She objects because she was informed before approving the work.
questions.explanation: Not negates the passive informing event, so the objection is to its absence, not to receiving information.
feedback: Being told gives her the recipient role; she is not the person disclosing the increase.
Not negates the passive informing event, so the objection is to its absence, not to receiving information.
The complaint concerns her own missing information, not withholding information from others.
Not being told and the timeline establish the opposite sequence.

questions.setup: A published account distorted the analyst's remarks before he had approved its wording. At the hearing, the record states: 'He denied resenting having been misquoted.'
questions.prompt: Which account preserves both the documented event and the scope of his denial?
options: He disputed the allegation that the published account had misquoted him.
He admitted resenting the misquotation but denied approving its wording beforehand.
He denied regretting his own earlier misquotation of someone else's remarks.
He disputed feeling resentment about the documented misquotation.
questions.explanation: 'Denied' takes scope over 'resenting'; the perfect passive gerund names the earlier treatment about which he denies feeling resentment.
feedback: The denial concerns resentment, not the documented misquotation named inside that emotional response.
This turns the denied emotion into an admission and moves the denial to approval.
The passive 'having been misquoted' makes him the person misrepresented, not the author of a misquotation.
'Denied' takes scope over 'resenting'; the perfect passive gerund names the earlier treatment about which he denies feeling resentment.

questions.setup: Read the reviewer's assessment. Choose the relation between the -ing clause and the main claim.
questions.prompt: 'Far from resolving the disagreement, the new definition introduces another ambiguity.'
options: The new ambiguity is the method used to resolve the disagreement.
The reviewer predicts a resolution after the new ambiguity is removed.
The reviewer rejects the claimed resolution and reports a new problem.
The disagreement was resolved before the new definition introduced ambiguity.
questions.explanation: Far from + -ing rejects an expected characterization; the main clause supplies the contrasting assessment.
feedback: Far from resolving denies the resolution rather than explaining how it was achieved.
No later resolution is predicted by this contrast.
Far from + -ing rejects an expected characterization; the main clause supplies the contrasting assessment.
The sentence does not assert any completed resolution; far from explicitly resists that claim.

questions.setup: The team assigned entry checks to assistants in an attempt to reduce errors. Choose the rewrite making these roles explicit without asserting successful error reduction.
questions.prompt: Original: 'To reduce errors, the entries were checked by assistants.'
options: The assistants had the team check the entries to reduce errors.
The team had assistants check the entries in an effort to reduce errors.
The team reduced errors by having assistants check the entries.
The team checked the entries so that assistants could reduce errors.
questions.explanation: This names the team's purpose and the assistants' action while leaving the outcome of error reduction unstated.
feedback: This reverses who arranged the checking and who performed it.
This names the team's purpose and the assistants' action while leaving the outcome of error reduction unstated.
This asserts successful error reduction, whereas the original states a purpose.
This assigns the checking to the team and makes error reduction the assistants' later action.

questions.setup: A historian writes, 'Lena's refusal to be questioned by the investigator delayed the inquiry.'
questions.prompt: Which rewrite preserves the participants and the reported reason for the delay?
options: The inquiry was delayed because Lena declined to undergo questioning by the investigator.
The inquiry was delayed because Lena declined to question the investigator.
The inquiry was delayed because Lena denied having been questioned by the investigator.
The inquiry was delayed while the investigator reluctantly answered Lena's questions.
questions.explanation: The passive infinitive in the original assigns Lena the recipient role; this rewrite retains that role and the refusal as the cause of delay.
feedback: The passive infinitive in the original assigns Lena the recipient role; this rewrite retains that role and the refusal as the cause of delay.
This makes Lena the intended questioner instead of the intended recipient of the questions.
A denial about a past event is not the refusal of questioning expressed in the original.
This reverses the roles and asserts that questioning occurred rather than reporting a refusal.

questions.setup: A deadline had been set before the researcher joined the project. Interpret the later complaint.
questions.prompt: 'She resented being expected to have completed the analysis before her first day.'
options: She admitted completing the analysis before joining and regretted that choice.
She expected someone else to finish the analysis before she joined.
She regretted setting a late deadline for another researcher's analysis.
She disliked the expectation of prior completion, not an established completion.
questions.explanation: Being expected places her under someone else's expectation; to have completed describes its earlier-time content without establishing that she fulfilled it.
feedback: The completion is content of an expectation, not an action she admits performing.
The passive being expected makes her the person expected to finish, not the person setting the expectation.
The sentence assigns her neither the deadline-setting role nor responsibility for someone else's work.
Being expected places her under someone else's expectation; to have completed describes its earlier-time content without establishing that she fulfilled it.

questions.setup: Compare the accounts as their narrators present them. Choose the distinction between the embedded actions.
questions.prompt: (1) 'Nico regretted having withheld the letter.' (2) 'Nico denied having withheld the letter.'
options: Both accounts establish that Nico withheld the letter and later regretted it.
Neither account presents any position on whether withholding occurred.
(1) presents withholding as a fact; (2) reports Nico's rejection of that claim.
(1) concerns future withholding; (2) concerns an earlier act of withholding.
questions.explanation: The same perfect gerund locates an earlier action, but regretted and denied give that action different evidential status.
feedback: Denied reports rejection of the claim and does not express regret.
Regretted treats the earlier act as something regretted; denied explicitly reports a position against the allegation.
The same perfect gerund locates an earlier action, but regretted and denied give that action different evidential status.
Having withheld gives earlier reference in both; the contrast is the main verb's stance.

questions.setup: A record says, 'Mara objected to the clerk's deliberately withholding the figures.' Replace the verb-like -ing clause with a noun phrase while preserving whose action was deliberate.
questions.prompt: Which revision keeps the modifier and participant roles attached to the same action?
options: Mara objected to the deliberate withholding of the figures by the clerk.
Mara made a deliberate objection to the clerk's withholding of the figures.
The clerk objected to the deliberate withholding of the figures by Mara.
Mara objected to the deliberate withholding of the clerk's figures.
questions.explanation: The noun phrase uses adjective 'deliberate', an of-phrase for what was withheld, and a by-phrase preserving the clerk as agent.
feedback: The noun phrase uses adjective 'deliberate', an of-phrase for what was withheld, and a by-phrase preserving the clerk as agent.
This makes Mara's objection deliberate; the source specifically describes the clerk's withholding that way.
This swaps the objector and the person withholding the figures.
This identifies the clerk as owner of the figures but leaves the person withholding them unspecified.

questions.setup: A draft says, 'Marin's request to interview the curator was approved.' The intended applicant is Marin, who will ask the questions. Choose the clearest rewrite.
questions.prompt: Make the interviewer explicit while retaining approval of the request.
options: Marin was given permission to be interviewed by the curator.
The curator agreed to ask Marin to conduct an interview.
Marin approved the curator's request for an interview.
Marin was given permission to interview the curator.
questions.explanation: Marin is explicitly the person permitted to act, and the curator remains the interviewee.
feedback: This reverses the interviewer's and interviewee's roles.
This introduces a request by the curator and does not preserve Marin's approved request.
This makes Marin the approver and the curator the requester.
Marin is explicitly the person permitted to act, and the curator remains the interviewee.

questions.setup: Choose the rewrite preserving avoidance of waking the patient as the visitor's purpose. Do not assert whether the patient woke.
questions.prompt: 'The visitor spoke quietly in order not to wake the patient.'
options: The visitor spoke quietly to avoid waking the patient.
The visitor did not speak quietly in order to wake the patient.
The visitor spoke quietly and therefore did not wake the patient.
The visitor avoided speaking quietly so that the patient would not wake.
questions.explanation: Avoid waking preserves the negative purpose without asserting its success.
feedback: Avoid waking preserves the negative purpose without asserting its success.
This negates a purpose or the quiet speaking; it does not clearly state the purpose of avoiding waking.
This adds a successful outcome, which a purpose phrase alone does not establish.
This reverses the chosen behavior by saying quiet speech was avoided.

questions.setup: Compare what the two constructions attribute to Asha. Choose the accurate distinction.
questions.prompt: (1) 'It was considerate of Asha to wait.' (2) 'It was convenient for Asha to wait.'
options: Both sentences praise Asha's character for putting others first.
(1) says waiting suited her schedule; (2) praises her treatment of others.
(1) describes others waiting for Asha; (2) describes Asha herself waiting.
(1) evaluates her conduct; (2) says waiting suited her circumstances.
questions.explanation: Of links considerate to the person's conduct; for identifies the person for whom the action is convenient.
feedback: Convenient for evaluates how the action fits her circumstances, not her consideration for others.
This reverses the functions of considerate of and convenient for.
Asha is the person who waits in both sentences; the contrast concerns evaluation, not the actor.
Of links considerate to the person's conduct; for identifies the person for whom the action is convenient.

questions.setup: A reviewer has compared the final report with the comment log and writes the following. Choose the claim at the same degree of certainty.
questions.prompt: 'The authors appear to have failed to incorporate the final correction.'
options: The authors have proved that they attempted the correction unsuccessfully.
The evidence suggests that the correction was not incorporated.
The authors refuse to incorporate the correction in a future revision.
The authors appear to have incorporated the correction before it was requested.
questions.explanation: Appear qualifies the inference; to have failed places the apparent non-performance earlier, while to incorporate names the missing action.
feedback: Appear does not establish proof, and failed to does not establish an attempt.
Appear qualifies the inference; to have failed places the apparent non-performance earlier, while to incorporate names the missing action.
The sentence concerns an apparent earlier omission, not a future refusal.
This reverses the failure and adds a timing claim not made in the original.

questions.setup: Read the editor's assessment. Choose the intended contrast.
questions.prompt: 'The revision involves not so much clarifying the exception as quietly widening it.'
options: The revision is better described as widening the exception than clarifying it.
The revision first clarifies the exception and then widens it.
The revision clarifies and widens the exception to exactly the same extent.
The revision neither clarifies nor widens the exception.
questions.explanation: Not so much X as Y corrects or reweights a description; it need not deny every trace of X.
feedback: Not so much X as Y corrects or reweights a description; it need not deny every trace of X.
The construction contrasts characterizations, not stages in a time sequence.
Not so much ... as gives greater weight to widening rather than equal weight.
The second characterization is asserted as the better account, not denied.

questions.setup: Compare (1) 'Judging from the photograph, the roof needs attention' and (2) 'To judge from the photograph, the roof needs attention.' An editor questions whether the roof is being made the judge.
questions.prompt: Which analysis best accounts for these two openings?
options: Both require an I-subject because any initial nonfinite clause must name an action of the main subject.
The first allows a speaker's assessment, but the second gives the roof a purpose of judging the photograph.
The first reports that the roof has already been assessed, while the second says assessment is still intended.
