questions.setup: Even in a quiet month, the studio still pays rent and insurance. These overheads put pressure on the business.
questions.prompt: What does 'overheads' mean here?
options: the selling price of each completed design
ongoing costs of running the business
the profit left after expenses
the extra charge for a single rush order
questions.explanation: Overheads are general operating costs, not costs tied solely to one particular job.
feedback: Selling prices are income terms, not rent and insurance costs.
Overheads are general operating costs, not costs tied solely to one particular job.
Overheads are expenses to be paid, not the remaining profit.
A rush surcharge is linked to a specific order, unlike these ongoing costs.

questions.setup: During onboarding, new employees receive system access, meet their teams and learn how the organization works.
questions.prompt: What is the purpose of onboarding?
options: helping new employees become established in the organization
selecting which applicants should receive offers
reviewing whether long-serving staff should be promoted
transferring an entire service to an outside company
questions.explanation: Onboarding introduces new staff to the practical and social aspects of their roles.
feedback: Onboarding introduces new staff to the practical and social aspects of their roles.
Recruitment selects applicants; these people are already new employees.
Onboarding supports entrants, not promotion reviews for established staff.
That is outsourcing, not settling new employees into work.

questions.setup: The cafe's sales revenue rose, but higher ingredient costs left it with less profit.
questions.prompt: Which distinction explains how both statements can be true?
options: Revenue excludes sales to regular customers.
Profit is counted before the cafe pays its costs.
Revenue is sales income; profit allows for costs.
Revenue and profit name the same amount.
questions.explanation: Revenue measures income from sales here, whereas profit depends on costs as well.
feedback: Sales revenue includes those sales; customer frequency is not the distinction.
Profit is what remains after relevant costs, not before them.
Revenue measures income from sales here, whereas profit depends on costs as well.
The sentence contrasts sales income with what remains after costs.

questions.setup: 'Procurement has asked us to compare three quotes before ordering,' the office manager said.
questions.prompt: Who or what does 'Procurement' refer to here?
options: the team responsible for obtaining goods and services
the goods that have already arrived
the customer waiting for the finished product
the payment sent to the chosen supplier
questions.explanation: A department's function can stand for its staff; Procurement here means the buying team.
feedback: A department's function can stand for its staff; Procurement here means the buying team.
Goods cannot ask the manager to compare quotes.
The quotation request comes from the organization's purchasing function.
A payment cannot issue the request, and selection has not yet occurred.

questions.setup: The designers finish twenty labels a day, but the single reviewer can approve only five. The director calls approval the bottleneck.
questions.prompt: What does 'bottleneck' identify?
options: the stage requiring the most expensive equipment
the task considered most important to customers
the stage producing the largest amount of completed work
the stage restricting overall throughput
questions.explanation: A bottleneck restricts overall throughput because work cannot pass through it quickly enough.
feedback: Equipment cost is not the limiting factor described.
Importance is not the defining feature; the approval capacity limits output.
Design produces more, but approval constrains what can move onward.
A bottleneck restricts overall throughput because work cannot pass through it quickly enough.

questions.setup: A supplier quotes a six-week lead time for custom desks, although making each desk takes only two days.
questions.prompt: How can these statements be consistent?
options: Lead time measures how long the desks should last.
Lead time excludes the time before production starts.
It includes waiting as well as manufacture.
The quoted six weeks describes the desk's assembly labor alone.
questions.explanation: Commercial lead time includes the time needed before an order can be fulfilled, which may extend beyond active production.
feedback: Expected useful life is different from the waiting period before supply.
Lead time can include waiting for materials or a production slot.
Commercial lead time includes the time needed before an order can be fulfilled, which may extend beyond active production.
The contrast with two days shows a broader order-to-fulfilment interval.

questions.setup: The design team's remit covers packaging, not the product recipe. It referred a proposed ingredient change to product development.
questions.prompt: What does 'remit' delimit?
options: the matters the team is assigned to handle
the hours during which the team is available
the skills individual designers happen to possess
the amount the team has spent on packaging
questions.explanation: A team's remit is its assigned area of responsibility or authority.
feedback: A team's remit is its assigned area of responsibility or authority.
Working hours concern availability, not the subject area assigned to the team.
Someone may have skills beyond the team's remit; the term concerns assigned responsibility.
Expenditure is not the boundary of responsibility named here.

questions.setup: Before changing delivery hours, the depot consulted drivers, neighboring residents and major customers as stakeholders.
questions.prompt: Which description explains the residents' stakeholder status?
options: They have acquired an ownership share in the depot.
They have been given authority to decide the depot's hours.
They are parties to the depot's delivery contracts.
Their interests may be affected by the depot's decision.
questions.explanation: Stakeholders have an interest in or are affected by an activity; ownership is not required.
feedback: Stakeholders need not be shareholders; consultation does not establish ownership.
Being affected and consulted does not establish decision-making authority.
Residents can be stakeholders without being customers or contracting parties.
Stakeholders have an interest in or are affected by an activity; ownership is not required.

questions.setup: The editor changed the workflow so illustrations reach the layout team before text is finalized. The number of assignments stayed the same.
questions.prompt: What changed, rather than the workload?
options: the amount of work assigned to each employee
the range of benefits offered to the staff
the organization and passage of work between stages
the total number of publications commissioned
questions.explanation: Workflow concerns the organization and movement of work through stages.
feedback: The sentence distinguishes organization of work from the amount of work.
Benefits concern employment conditions, not how illustrations reach layout.
Workflow concerns the organization and movement of work through stages.
Assignment numbers are unchanged; workflow does not mean total commissioned output.

questions.setup: A vacancy lists a full-time salary of $40,000, pro rata for part-time hours.
questions.prompt: What does 'pro rata' tell a part-time applicant about the advertised figure?
options: The amount is adjusted in proportion to the hours worked.
It is the minimum regardless of hours worked.
It is paid only as a bonus after the first year.
It will be negotiated without reference to working hours.
questions.explanation: Pro rata means in proportion; here the full-time figure is scaled to the agreed working hours.
feedback: Pro rata means in proportion; here the full-time figure is scaled to the agreed working hours.
Pro rata indicates proportional adjustment, not the same guaranteed amount for all hours.
The phrase concerns proportion, not a performance bonus or waiting period.
The advertisement explicitly links the proportion to part-time hours.

questions.setup: The publisher plans to reduce staffing through attrition rather than compulsory redundancies.
questions.prompt: Which approach does 'through attrition' describe?
options: Staff are dismissed and replaced by junior employees.
Employees keep their posts but work fewer hours.
Staff leave and their posts remain unfilled.
Departing employees are replaced by outside contractors.
questions.explanation: Attrition reduces staff as people leave and their positions are not filled.
feedback: Dismissal followed by replacement is not reducing staff through attrition.
Reduced hours retain the posts; attrition here reduces staff numbers through departures.
Attrition reduces staff as people leave and their positions are not filled.
Substituting contractors for departing employees describes outsourcing rather than simple non-replacement.

questions.setup: A British employer announced redundancies after closing its print room, while thanking the affected staff for their excellent work.
questions.prompt: Which interpretation explains why the thanks and redundancies are compatible?
options: Redundancy means a temporary break until printing restarts.
The jobs, not their performance, are the issue.
Redundancy means the employees chose to retire.
The employees are being promoted into more senior posts.
questions.explanation: In British employment usage, redundancy concerns jobs no longer required, not necessarily the workers' performance.
feedback: Redundancy concerns losing an unneeded job, not necessarily a temporary absence.
In British employment usage, redundancy concerns jobs no longer required, not necessarily the workers' performance.
Voluntary retirement is a different employment event.
Redundancy is not a promotion, even when the employees' work is praised.

questions.setup: After informal discussions failed, an employee lodged a grievance about how shift preferences had been allocated.
questions.prompt: What change does 'lodged a grievance' signal?
options: The employee has submitted a formal complaint.
The employee has accepted the allocation.
The employer has confirmed that the complaint is justified.
The employee has resigned from the organization.
questions.explanation: To lodge a grievance is to submit a formal workplace complaint.
feedback: To lodge a grievance is to submit a formal workplace complaint.
A grievance contests perceived unfair treatment rather than accepts it.
Submitting a grievance does not establish its outcome.
A complaint can be pursued while the employee remains in the job.

questions.setup: The project plan lists 'prototype accepted' as a milestone and 'a working prototype with instructions' as a deliverable.
questions.prompt: What distinguishes the deliverable?
options: It is the amount of time the team expects to spend.
It is any event the team considers encouraging.
It is the specified output the team must provide.
It is the person responsible for approval.
questions.explanation: A deliverable is an agreed product or result; a milestone marks a significant point or achievement.
feedback: Effort or duration is an input, not the product handed over.
A deliverable is an agreed output, not simply a positive event.
A deliverable is an agreed product or result; a milestone marks a significant point or achievement.
The approver is a role, whereas the deliverable is a result of work.

questions.setup: Unable to approve the requested exception herself, the coordinator escalated the issue to the operations director.
questions.prompt: What does 'escalated' mean here?
options: made the disagreement deliberately more hostile
referred it to someone with greater authority
increased the size of the requested exception
withdrew the issue from consideration
questions.explanation: In a workplace process, escalating an issue can mean referring it to a higher decision-making level.
feedback: Escalate can describe worsening conflict, but this sentence identifies referral to a director.
In a workplace process, escalating an issue can mean referring it to a higher decision-making level.
The requested exception is unchanged; its decision-maker changes.
Referral continues consideration rather than ending it.

questions.setup: The sales target remains ambitious, but the forecast has been revised down after several customers delayed orders.
questions.prompt: Which distinction between target and forecast is maintained?
options: The target estimates likely sales; the forecast sets an ambition.
The target expresses ambition; the forecast estimates results.
The target is a minimum acceptable result; the forecast promises an amount.
The target sets the intended result; the forecast records completed orders.
questions.explanation: A target states what an organization aims for; a forecast estimates what is likely under current conditions.
feedback: That reverses the terms: a target is the aim, while a forecast estimates the outcome.
A target states what an organization aims for; a forecast estimates what is likely under current conditions.
Targets need not be minimum acceptable results, and forecasts estimate rather than promise.
The target description fits, but a forecast is forward-looking rather than a record of completed business.

questions.setup: The bakery kept its selling prices unchanged while flour and butter became more expensive. Its gross margin narrowed.
questions.prompt: What does 'narrowed' say about the gross margin?
options: The bakery sold a smaller range of products.
The bakery had less physical room for production.
Less remained from sales after the cost of goods sold.
Customers received a larger price discount.
questions.explanation: A narrower gross margin means a smaller gap between sales income and the cost of the goods sold.
feedback: Product range is not the margin between sales income and the relevant cost of goods.
Margin here is a financial measure, not workspace.
A narrower gross margin means a smaller gap between sales income and the cost of the goods sold.
Selling prices were unchanged; higher costs explain the reduced margin.

questions.setup: The booking system preserves an audit trail even after a reservation is edited.
questions.prompt: What should an investigator be able to use that trail for?
options: restoring every deleted file to its original device
preventing staff from making any further edits
proving that each edit was authorized and correct
tracing which changes were made, when and by whom
questions.explanation: An audit trail records a sequence of actions so changes can be traced.
feedback: That is a backup function; an audit trail need not contain full restorable files.
A trail records actions; it does not necessarily prevent them.
Recording an action does not establish that it was proper.
An audit trail records a sequence of actions so changes can be traced.

questions.setup: Our counterparty suggested a change to the supply agreement, and we accepted it without dispute.
questions.prompt: What does 'counterparty' identify without implying hostility?
options: the other party to the agreement
an independent observer with no part in the agreement
a competitor trying to prevent the agreement
our own employee responsible for checking the figures
questions.explanation: A counterparty is the other participant in an agreement or transaction; the relationship need not be adversarial.
feedback: A counterparty is the other participant in an agreement or transaction; the relationship need not be adversarial.
An observer is not a party to the transaction.
The other contracting party is not necessarily a market competitor or opponent.
Counterparty refers to the other side, not an internal checker.

questions.setup: Before going on leave, the project lead arranged a handover with her deputy. The project itself will continue for months.
questions.prompt: What is the handover intended to achieve?
options: mark the completion of all project work
confirm that the deputy has become the permanent project lead
submit the final product to the customer
pass on responsibilities and the information needed
questions.explanation: A handover passes work or responsibility to another person, usually with relevant information.
feedback: The project is continuing; handover does not mean completion.
Temporary leave does not establish a permanent appointment.
This handover is between colleagues and concerns continuing work, not final client delivery.
A handover passes work or responsibility to another person, usually with relevant information.

questions.setup: The team used last year's response time as a benchmark. Its new target is faster still.
questions.prompt: What role does last year's figure play?
options: It is a reference point against which performance can be compared.
It specifies the team's new response-time goal.
It identifies the best response time achieved in the industry.
It establishes a minimum standard acceptable to customers.
questions.explanation: A benchmark provides a basis for comparison; it need not be the current target.
feedback: A benchmark provides a basis for comparison; it need not be the current target.
The new target is faster; last year's figure serves a different comparison role.
The benchmark comes from this team's previous year, not an industry-wide record.
The report identifies a comparison basis, not a customer-defined threshold.

questions.setup: A supplier closure is one contingency in the event plan; using a second supplier is the proposed response.
questions.prompt: What does 'contingency' name here?
options: the backup supplier already booked
the event's ordinary day-to-day schedule
the confirmed reason the event has been cancelled
a possible event the organizers need to prepare for
questions.explanation: Contingency can name an event that may occur; a contingency plan specifies how to respond.
feedback: The backup response is separate from the possible closure.
A contingency is a possible eventuality, not the routine timetable.
No closure or cancellation is confirmed; the plan anticipates a possibility.
Contingency can name an event that may occur; a contingency plan specifies how to respond.

questions.setup: A website redesign gradually acquired extra pages and reporting tools through casual requests, with no revised brief. The developer warned of scope creep.
questions.prompt: What problem does 'scope creep' identify?
options: The agreed work is being completed faster than expected.
Unmanaged requests are expanding the agreed work.
The original requirements are being deliberately reduced.
The team has formally approved a new project brief.
questions.explanation: Scope creep is the gradual, unmanaged expansion of a project's requirements.
feedback: The concern is expanding requirements, not improved speed.
Scope creep is the gradual, unmanaged expansion of a project's requirements.
Additional pages and tools expand rather than reduce the work.
The absence of a revised brief distinguishes uncontrolled expansion from an agreed change.

questions.setup: The college is inviting tenders for catering. A supplier asks whether this means the contract has already been awarded.
questions.prompt: Which answer accurately distinguishes the stages?
options: Yes; inviting tenders confirms that one supplier has been chosen.
No; suppliers are being asked to submit formal offers for consideration.
Yes; every supplier who responds receives part of the contract.
No; suppliers are only being asked to submit bills for completed work.
questions.explanation: A tender is a formal offer to provide work or supplies; inviting tenders precedes selection.
feedback: Inviting offers begins competition rather than announcing the selected supplier.
A tender is a formal offer to provide work or supplies; inviting tenders precedes selection.
Responding with a tender does not guarantee any award.
Bills seek payment for work; tenders offer to undertake it.

questions.setup: The buyer's due diligence uncovered an unreliable customer database, prompting a lower offer rather than abandonment of the purchase.
questions.prompt: What role did due diligence play?
options: It certified that the business was free from material weaknesses.
It set the seller's asking price independently of the buyer.
It investigated the business to inform the buyer's decision.
It monitored the buyer's performance after the acquisition.
questions.explanation: Due diligence is pre-decision investigation; adverse findings may alter terms rather than end the transaction.
feedback: The investigation found a weakness; due diligence is not a certificate of perfection.
The buyer used the findings to revise its own offer; the process does not set the seller's price.
Due diligence is pre-decision investigation; adverse findings may alter terms rather than end the transaction.
The offer was still being reconsidered, so this was investigation before purchase, not later monitoring.

questions.setup: A purchasing manager disclosed that a bidder was her brother's company. The report noted a conflict of interest, without finding that she had favored it.
questions.prompt: Which interpretation preserves the distinction being made?
options: A competing interest exists, without a finding of favoritism.
The competing suppliers had a disagreement that the manager needed to settle.
The disclosure established that the company submitted a dishonest bid.
The manager's family connection was irrelevant once it had been disclosed.
questions.explanation: A conflict of interest concerns potentially competing duties or interests, distinct from proof that someone acted improperly.
feedback: A conflict of interest concerns potentially competing duties or interests, distinct from proof that someone acted improperly.
This conflict is between the manager's role and personal connection, not between bidders.
A family connection does not itself establish dishonesty in the bid.
Disclosure reveals the conflict; it does not make the competing interest disappear.

questions.setup: Funds for accessibility work are ring-fenced. The operations manager cannot divert them to cover a routine stationery shortfall.
questions.prompt: What does 'ring-fenced' add beyond saying the funds exist?
options: The funds have already been paid to an accessibility contractor.
The funds are available to whichever department first requests them.
The amount is expected to rise with stationery prices.
Their use is restricted to the designated purpose.
questions.explanation: Ring-fenced funds are protected from diversion to other uses; availability is not unrestricted permission to spend.
feedback: Restriction of use does not mean expenditure has already occurred.
Ring-fencing reserves the funds for a specified purpose rather than general competition.
The term concerns protected purpose, not automatic changes in value.
Ring-fenced funds are protected from diversion to other uses; availability is not unrestricted permission to spend.

questions.setup: Under matrix management, engineers answer to a technical lead for professional standards and to project leads for delivery priorities.
questions.prompt: Which issue is characteristic of this arrangement?
options: Overlapping authorities may create priorities that need reconciling.
Every decision must pass through a single unbroken line of command.
Project leads replace technical standards with personal preferences.
Engineers become external suppliers instead of employees.
questions.explanation: Matrix management combines dimensions of authority, such as function and project, so priorities may require coordination.
feedback: Matrix management combines dimensions of authority, such as function and project, so priorities may require coordination.
The arrangement describes overlapping reporting relationships rather than one exclusive hierarchy.
Having project authority does not remove the technical lead's standards.
The reporting structure does not change them into outside contractors.

questions.setup: The team delivered the agreed three prototypes. Its manager then said success required five and was accused of moving the goalposts.
questions.prompt: What is the specific criticism?
options: He announced a difficult target before the work began.
He changed the agreed test of success retrospectively.
He used the wrong measure to compare two unrelated products.
He accepted a lower standard because the team was under pressure.
questions.explanation: Moving the goalposts criticizes changing the conditions of success after others have relied on them.
feedback: The objection concerns a later change, not merely the difficulty of the original target.
Moving the goalposts criticizes changing the conditions of success after others have relied on them.
The measure remains prototype quantity; the required number changed.
He raised the requirement rather than relaxed it.

questions.setup: The director approved the new rota, but the supervisors doubted it would work and avoided planning around it. The project lacked buy-in.
questions.prompt: What was missing despite formal approval?
options: money to purchase scheduling software
a document proving the director had authority
an external company willing to operate the rota
commitment from the people implementing the change
questions.explanation: Buy-in is practical support for an idea or course of action, distinct from permission at the top.
feedback: Buy-in here is not literally buying a product or funding a purchase.
The director's approval is given; buy-in concerns participants' commitment.
A supplier contract is not the internal support described by buy-in.
Buy-in is practical support for an idea or course of action, distinct from permission at the top.

questions.setup: The buyer was flexible about delivery dates but described independent safety testing as a red line in the negotiations.
questions.prompt: What status does the testing requirement have for the buyer?
options: It is a condition she is unwilling to concede.
It is an opening request she expects to trade away.
It is a useful preference subordinate to getting an earlier delivery.
It is an issue she has deliberately left for later discussion.
questions.explanation: In negotiation, a red line is a limit a party will not accept crossing.
feedback: In negotiation, a red line is a limit a party will not accept crossing.
A red line marks a limit she does not intend to cross, not a routine bargaining concession.
Calling it a red line makes it a boundary, unlike the flexible delivery dates.
The phrase establishes a position on the requirement rather than postponing one.

questions.setup: The review panel approved every request within a minute, without opening the supporting files. Staff called it a rubber stamp.
questions.prompt: What does the description criticize?
options: The panel lacked any authority to approve requests.
The panel rejected requests without giving reasons.
Approval had become perfunctory rather than a genuine examination.
The requests were processed on paper rather than electronically.
questions.explanation: Calling a body a rubber stamp suggests it routinely approves decisions without substantive independent consideration.
feedback: A panel may have formal authority while using it without meaningful scrutiny.
It approved every request; the criticism is insufficient scrutiny, not unexplained rejection.
Calling a body a rubber stamp suggests it routinely approves decisions without substantive independent consideration.
The expression is figurative and does not specify the medium.

questions.setup: The bonus policy includes a clawback if the results used to calculate an award later prove inaccurate.
questions.prompt: What action does 'clawback' refer to, without deciding whether it applies in a particular case?
options: increasing future bonuses to correct an underestimate
recovering an award already paid or granted
deferring an award that has not yet become payable
replacing a performance award with ordinary wages
questions.explanation: A clawback provision permits recovery in specified circumstances; the word itself does not establish that those circumstances occurred.
feedback: A clawback recovers value, rather than increases a later award.
A clawback provision permits recovery in specified circumstances; the word itself does not establish that those circumstances occurred.
Deferral postpones payment; clawback concerns recovering an award already made.
Changing the type of pay is not the recovery described by clawback.

questions.setup: Rehearsals and costume work can overlap, but the stage must be built before lighting can be fitted. The build and lighting work lie on the production's critical path.
questions.prompt: What does 'critical path' identify?
options: the tasks with the least spare money in their budgets
the activities demanding the greatest total staff-hours
the sequence determining the earliest overall finish
the sequence ending at the earliest internal milestone
questions.explanation: In project planning, the critical path determines minimum overall duration; delaying an activity on it delays completion unless the plan changes.
feedback: Limited budget is a financial constraint; the critical path is defined by scheduling dependencies and duration.
Labor effort and elapsed duration differ; a labor-intensive task need not control the overall finish.
In project planning, the critical path determines minimum overall duration; delaying an activity on it delays completion unless the plan changes.
The critical path determines the overall project's duration, not simply the earliest intermediate milestone.

questions.setup: While a separate team replaces the stock system, store staff are expected to maintain business as usual.
questions.prompt: What does 'business as usual' ask store staff to sustain?
options: the existing stock software indefinitely
exactly the same staffing and sales figures every day
normal operations despite the change happening alongside them
a pause in customer service until the replacement is complete
questions.explanation: Business as usual refers to ordinary ongoing activity, even when a separate change is underway.
feedback: The software is being replaced; the phrase does not cancel that change.
Routine operation does not mean all numerical measures remain identical.
Business as usual refers to ordinary ongoing activity, even when a separate change is underway.
Business as usual calls for continuity rather than a service pause.

questions.setup: The departure agreement lists final salary, outstanding expenses and a separate severance payment.
questions.prompt: What distinguishes the severance payment in this list?
options: It repays the employee's travel and other work costs.
It is ordinary pay for work already completed.
It is the salary promised by the employee's next employer.
It is compensation connected with the ending of employment.
questions.explanation: Severance pay is connected with separation from employment, distinct from earned salary and expense repayment.
feedback: Those are listed separately as outstanding expenses.
That is the separately listed final salary.
The payment belongs to the departure arrangement, not a future job offer.
Severance pay is connected with separation from employment, distinct from earned salary and expense repayment.

questions.setup: Two teams in the same consultancy serve competing clients. An information barrier restricts access to their respective client files.
questions.prompt: What does the barrier separate?
options: the firms' buildings so their staff cannot meet socially
the teams into independent companies with separate owners
access to sensitive information, not necessarily physical workplaces
the quality standards used for the two clients
questions.explanation: An information barrier controls information sharing; teams can be in one organization or location.
feedback: The control concerns information access, not a ban on social contact.
Information controls do not by themselves change company ownership.
An information barrier controls information sharing; teams can be in one organization or location.
Standards can remain shared while client information is separated.

questions.setup: Representatives of the drivers met management to negotiate a pay agreement covering the group. The talks were described as collective bargaining.
questions.prompt: Which feature makes this collective bargaining rather than individual negotiation?
options: Every employee negotiates a private agreement at the same time.
Representatives negotiate employment terms on behalf of a group.
Management announces a completed decision to the workforce.
Employees exchange opinions without negotiating with the employer.
questions.explanation: Collective bargaining concerns negotiations between an employer and workers' representatives over group employment terms.
feedback: Parallel individual deals would not be the group agreement described.
Collective bargaining concerns negotiations between an employer and workers' representatives over group employment terms.
Bargaining involves negotiating terms, not merely communicating a decision.
An internal discussion among workers lacks the employer-side negotiation described.

questions.setup: An engineer reported suspected falsification of test results through the company's internal reporting channel. The account calls her a whistleblower.
questions.prompt: Which interpretation fits that description without adding an unsupported claim?
options: She reported suspected wrongdoing through an internal channel.
She has already proved the falsification in an independent hearing.
She must have sent the information to the press.
She was appointed to negotiate compensation for the workforce.
questions.explanation: Whistleblower identifies someone reporting wrongdoing; it does not require a public disclosure or prove the allegation.
feedback: Whistleblower identifies someone reporting wrongdoing; it does not require a public disclosure or prove the allegation.
Reporting suspected wrongdoing does not itself establish a completed finding.
Whistleblowing can use an internal reporting channel, as this account states.
Representing workers in pay talks is different from reporting suspected wrongdoing.

questions.setup: The induction required staff to click through every safety slide, but no one checked their understanding. A supervisor called it a box-ticking exercise.
questions.prompt: What does that criticism target?
options: the use of written records in any effective training program
the choice of safety as an inappropriate subject for induction
the absence of a formally specified training process
completion of formal steps taking priority over their practical purpose
questions.explanation: A box-ticking exercise satisfies visible requirements without sufficient attention to the underlying aim.
feedback: The phrase criticizes superficial compliance here, not all record-keeping.
The criticism concerns how safety learning was handled, not its relevance.
A formal process exists; the concern is that completing it may not produce understanding.
A box-ticking exercise satisfies visible requirements without sufficient attention to the underlying aim.

questions.setup: Although the two suppliers share premises, they insist their commercial dealings are conducted at arm's length.
questions.prompt: What are they claiming about those dealings?
options: They occur without any direct communication.
They concern only customers located far from the shared premises.
They are conducted in an atmosphere of personal hostility.
They deal independently rather than giving one another special treatment.
questions.explanation: An arm's-length relationship means dealing as independent parties, without preferential treatment arising from closeness.
feedback: Independent dealing can involve frequent direct communication.
Arm's length is not a measure of geographical distance.
Independence does not require hostility or an adversarial tone.
An arm's-length relationship means dealing as independent parties, without preferential treatment arising from closeness.

questions.setup: Rather than nominate one permanent heir to the director, the firm developed several managers for different future leadership needs as part of succession planning.
questions.prompt: What is the central aim of this planning?
options: filling an immediately vacant post through an external advertisement
preparing continuity of leadership rather than guaranteeing one person's promotion
rewarding past performance with a permanent right to the director's job
redistributing the current director's daily tasks while she is on leave
questions.explanation: Succession planning develops readiness for future leadership transitions; it need not promise a named individual a role.
feedback: Succession planning can be forward-looking development, not merely immediate vacancy recruitment.
Succession planning develops readiness for future leadership transitions; it need not promise a named individual a role.
Preparation for possible leadership is not an irrevocable entitlement.
A temporary handover addresses immediate cover, not longer-term leadership succession.

questions.setup: Only one technician knows how to restore the booking database. She works quickly and accurately, but managers call this dependence a single point of failure.
questions.prompt: Why does the label fit despite her strong performance?
options: Her unavailability could disable a function with no workable alternative.
Her work is the slowest stage in the booking process.
She has repeatedly made serious restoration errors.
She is personally responsible for every fault in the database.
questions.explanation: A single point of failure is a dependency whose failure or loss can stop the wider function, even if it usually performs well.
feedback: A single point of failure is a dependency whose failure or loss can stop the wider function, even if it usually performs well.
She works quickly; the concern is dependence on her availability, not a bottleneck.
The account states she works accurately; the label does not imply a poor record.
A dependency risk does not assign blame for all failures.

questions.setup: The start-up has six months of runway at its current rate of net cash outflow, even though it has not yet earned a profit.
questions.prompt: Which reading captures 'runway' in this business update?
options: the time until its first profitable sale is guaranteed
how long cash can sustain operations at that rate
the period customers must wait for their orders
the total duration of its longest supplier contract
questions.explanation: Business runway describes how long available cash can sustain the net outflow under the stated conditions.
feedback: Runway estimates how long resources last, not when profit will arrive.
Business runway describes how long available cash can sustain the net outflow under the stated conditions.
Customer waiting time is lead time, not the company's cash runway.
Contract length does not determine the cash period described here.
